newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Police make arrest in Guatemala stadium tragedy.
newsitem.headline: Police make arrest in Guatemala stadium tragedy.

text.p: Police arrested on Monday one of 15 people charged with partial responsibility for a crush in an overcrowded stadium that killed 81 people during a World Cup qualifying soccer match in October.

"The arrest of Rene Arroyo is confirmed. The night of October 16 he headed a work group responsible for the doormen and for the people who had the keys to emergency doors," special prosecutor Selvin Galindo told reporters.
Galindo said a judge issued arrest orders for 14 other people linked to the stadium tragedy. But he did not name them.
Under Guatemala's legal system specific criminal charges are decided by the courts after an arrest.

On the night of the tragedy, half an hour before kickoff of the game between Guatemala and Costa Rica in Mateo Flores stadium an unknown event in the packed, standing-room-only terraces at one end of the stadium triggered a human avalanche.

People died crushed under each other half way up the concrete bleachers. Investigators dismissed earlier reports that many of the victims died crushed against a fence that separated the stands from the field.

Three separate groups were investigating the disaster: the team of prosecutors from the attorney general's office, a presidential commission scheduled to release a report later this week and a congressional commission.
Prosecutors and other investigators believe overcrowding and ticket forgery were the cause of the worst disaster in World Cup history.
Several different investigating teams are trying to establish the safe capacity of the stadium.

A ticket count which turned up more than 500 false tickets taken at stadium doors that night has established that the stadium was probably not crowded beyond it's historic capacity which different sports authorities have measured at different numbers from 45,000 to 48,000.
But following the disaster, new measurements of seating areas, aisles, and safety exits have established that the true capacity of the stadium may be closer to 32,000.
